title: Derived scalar localization is reflective with its normalized unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $s$ a global section. Put $S=R[1/s]$, the sheafified sectionwise localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q_R,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write $E(M)=S\otimes_R M$ and $U_0$ for ordinary extension and restriction. Let $F=S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $U$ be derived restriction, with the evaluation-normalized adjunction $F\dashv U$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. Then $E,U_0$ are exact, and there are natural identifications $F(Q_RM)\cong Q_S(E M)$ and $U(Q_SN)\cong Q_R(U_0N)$ for every complex $M$ over $R$ and $N$ over $S$. In these identifications $\eta_{Q_RM}$ is represented by $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, and $\varepsilon_{Q_SN}$ by multiplication $S\otimes_R U_0N\to N$, $b\otimes x\mapsto bx$. The counit is an isomorphism for every $N\in D(S)$. For every $A\in D(R)$ and $N\in D(S)$, precomposition with $\eta_A$ is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(UFA,UN)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(A,UN),\qquad q\longmapsto q\circ\eta_A,$$
with inverse $h\longmapsto U\varepsilon_N\circ UF(h)$. In particular $UF(\eta_A)=\eta_{UFA}$. No boundedness or nonzero hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 03ET (lemma-flatness-sheafification), localization-flatness input; agent derived-reflection argument extracted from the returned parent proof steps 2–3, not a verbatim assertion of this tag. The full argument and derived-adjunction source are retained in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-sheaf-exact] to the given small ringed site and global section $s$: the actual sheafified scalar-extension functor $E$ is additive and exact. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction] to $R\to S$: $U_0$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits and $E\dashv U_0$ has Hom correspondence $f\mapsto(x\mapsto f(1\otimes x))$. Taking $f=1_{EM}$ gives the ordinary unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$; the inverse correspondence sends $g$ to $b\otimes x\mapsto b g(x)$, by the balancing relation and the universal property of the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Taking $g=1_{U_0N}$ gives the ordinary counit $\mu_N(b\otimes x)=bx$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], termwise $E$ and $U_0$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce functors $D(E),D(U_0)$ with natural factorizations $D(E)Q_R\cong Q_SE$ and $D(U_0)Q_S\cong Q_RU_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] the first factorization is a left derived functor and the second is a right derived functor, on the entire unbounded derived categories. The universal property defining the left derived functor identifies $D(E)$ canonically with $F$ of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]: the universal comparison maps in the two directions compose to the identity by uniqueness. The same argument identifies $D(U_0)$ with $U$ of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. These are the required natural identifications for every complex, without any boundedness restriction.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), with the dual left-derived assertion; canonical uniqueness of the derived pair.

proof.text: Apply the functors of step 1 degreewise. The displayed unit and multiplication counit are chain maps, since the differentials are linear. Localize these natural transformations using clauses (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] and the factorizations of step 2. The two triangle identities hold after precomposition with $Q_R$ or $Q_S$, because they are the ordinary identities in each degree; clause (3) therefore proves the triangle identities on the derived categories. This constructs an adjunction whose unit and counit on every complex are exactly the classes of those chain maps.

source.place: Tag 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), exact-functor case; explicit descent of unit, counit and triangle identities.

proof.text: Compare the descended adjunction with the specified evaluation-normalized one. The coefficient nodes write $P\otimes_R S$, whereas $E(P)=S\otimes_R P$. The maps $x\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes x$ and $b\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes b$ respect the balancing relations, restrictions and differentials, and are inverse; sheafification gives the natural comparison [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For a flat-term K-flat complex $P$, the comparison of step 2 agrees, through this switch, with the canonical K-flat comparison of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], since both are the comparison of the same universal derived pair. Clause (1) of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] therefore identifies its unit with the descended unit. For any complex $M$, choose $r:P\to M$ as in [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For either unit $\alpha$, naturality gives $\alpha_{Q_RM}=UF(Q_Rr)\circ\alpha_{Q_RP}\circ(Q_Rr)^{-1}$; hence the units agree at $Q_RM$. Essential surjectivity in [lem-sfb-derived-localization-additive] gives agreement everywhere. With fixed functors and unit, the Hom correspondence is $f\mapsto U(f)\circ\eta$, so the counit, its inverse image of the identity, also agrees. This proves both normalization formulas for arbitrary complexes.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); derived.tex Tags 015F and 0FND. Comparison through the common K-flat normalization.

proof.text: We check the ordinary multiplication counit is invertible, retaining the sheafification in $S$. Let $T$ be any $S$-module sheaf and put $j:T\to U_0E(U_0T)$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. This is an $R$-linear sheaf map. On both its source and target multiplication by $s$ is invertible, since they are $S$-modules. Consequently $j(s^{-1}x)=s^{-1}j(x)$, by applying the inverse of multiplication by $s$ to $j(sx)=s j(x)$. Hence $j$ is linear over the presheaf $B(V)=R(V)[1/s|_V]$. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], applied to $B\to B^\#=S$ of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], this map between sheaves is $S$-linear: both sheaves are their own underlying abelian sheafifications and the interface gives unique extension of $B$-linear maps to $S$-linear maps. Now $\mu_Tj(x)=x$, while $j\mu_T(b\otimes x)=j(bx)=b j(x)=b\otimes x$. The latter equality determines a sheaf tensor map by its defining universal property [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus $j$ is the inverse of $\mu_T$. This argument is natural in $T$.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules) and Section 03EK (section-tensor-product); explicit inverse using the principal fractions.

proof.text: For a complex $N$, naturality of the inverse maps $j_{N^r}$ of step 5 makes them commute with the differentials. Thus multiplication $E(U_0N)\to N$ is an isomorphism of complexes, and steps 3–4 identify its class with $\varepsilon_{Q_SN}$. For any $H\in D(S)$ choose an isomorphism $a:Q_SN\to H$ using [lem-sfb-derived-localization-additive]. Naturality gives $\varepsilon_H=a\circ\varepsilon_{Q_SN}\circ(FU(a))^{-1}$, a composite of isomorphisms. Thus $\varepsilon$ is invertible on every derived object.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); termwise invertible counit, transported to every derived object.

proof.text: The left triangle identity is $\varepsilon_{FA}\circ F(\eta_A)=1_{FA}$. By step 6 it gives $F(\eta_A)=\varepsilon_{FA}^{-1}$. The right triangle identity at $FA$ gives $U(\varepsilon_{FA})\circ\eta_{UFA}=1_{UFA}$, hence $\eta_{UFA}=(U\varepsilon_{FA})^{-1}=UF(\eta_A)$. This proves the stated unit identity.

source.place: Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); elementary triangle-identity calculation for the adjunction constructed above.

proof.text: For $h:A\to UN$ define $\Psi(h)=U\varepsilon_N\circ UF(h)$. Naturality of $\eta$ and the right triangle identity give $\Psi(h)\circ\eta_A=U\varepsilon_N\circ\eta_{UN}\circ h=h$. Conversely, for $q:UFA\to UN$, step 7 and naturality give $\Psi(q\circ\eta_A)=U\varepsilon_N\circ UF(q)\circ UF(\eta_A)=U\varepsilon_N\circ UF(q)\circ\eta_{UFA}=U\varepsilon_N\circ\eta_{UN}\circ q=q$. These two equations prove the claimed bijection with precisely its displayed inverse. All preceding constructions are unbounded; if $s$ is zero or nilpotent then $S$ is the zero sheaf and the same equations still hold. No nonzero assumption was used.

source.place: Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); explicit inverse computations from naturality and the right triangle identity.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NO-40dcdd51c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all 8 steps in full, with every cited node statement. No new nodes and no repair note, so this is not a re-split. The statement, deps and blueprint are unchanged from cc37660e3385; only steps 4 and 6 were made explicit. Step 1: exactness of E comes from lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-sheaf-exact, and the ordinary unit and multiplication counit come from the ordinary-adjunction Hom formula plus balancing. Step 2: uniqueness of right Kan extensions identifies D(E) with Lφ*, and U is literally termwise Res. Step 3: the transformations are lifted and the triangle identities checked through localization-universal-property clauses (2) and (3). Step 4: the unit is matched with the normalized one on flat-term K-flat P via c_P and the tensor switch, then on every Q_R M through a K-flat resolution and naturality, then on every object by essential surjectivity; the counit follows from unit uniqueness. Step 5: j(x)=1⊗x commutes with s^{-1}, so it is B=R[1/s]-linear, and the 03CY interface makes it S-linear; μj=1 and jμ=1 are checked on pure tensors and extended through sheafification. This correctly avoids assuming S(V)=R(V)[1/s]. Step 6: invertibility extends to all of D(S) by conjugation. Steps 7–8: the triangle-identity and naturality algebra is verified, and it gives exactly the displayed inverse. Edge cases: s a unit, s zero or nilpotent (S=0), unbounded complexes. Sources checked: 03ET at l.4293, 03CZ at l.933, 03CY at l.815, 0FND at derived l.9517; the tag table agrees. No duplicate of a general node exists (only scheme-specific integral→rational special cases), there is no cycle, and both citers use exactly the stated clauses. All six tool_uses are accepted as generic.
